Charlotte.title: Charlotte
Charlotte.content:
Charlotte
Role:: player (MC)
Location::
Seen In:: 2025-07-22
Status:: no
Type:: player

Background
Graphic designer, quiet loner, insomnia sufferer
Charlotte was born in Townia, raised by her grandmother in the northernmost house of the town. Her parents left when she was a baby — no one talks about them much. When she was 9, she left with her grandmother to the city after a “strange accident” at the quarry. She’s never remembered what happened — only that there was fog.
She hasn’t returned since.
Until now.

Recent Activity
The Nightmares Begin
Months ago, Charlotte began having vivid, repeating nightmares:

Always set in a fog-covered version of Townia
Always following a child’s voice she never sees
Always ending with a massive eye opening beneath her

The dreams worsened — insomnia followed, and her grip on reality began to fray. Her last sketch at work was of a lighthouse she didn’t remember drawing.
She finally gave in and returned to Townia — desperate for answers, or peace.
Arrived to town

Notes

Fog exposure: no
Memory loss: no

Location/Beach.title: Beach
Location/Beach.content:
Beach
Type:: Location
Region::
Access::
Connected Locations::
Fog Presence::

📜 Description
Standing tall on the western cliff, the lighthouse is Townia’s highest structure — once a beacon for wayward fishing boats, now a pulsing anomaly. Its light no longer rotates normally; instead, it pulses in deliberate intervals, sometimes flickering to the rhythm of something unseen offshore. The ocean crashes violently below, and no one comes up here unless they must. The path to the lighthouse is steep and exposed, often swallowed by fog. Despite its height, the fog here seems denser than anywhere else in town.

🧠 Lore / History
Randal has not left the tower in months. He speaks of “eyes in the fog” and “boats without hulls.”  The light no longer attracts ships — instead, it repels them. Or something near them.  Some nights, the light fails to cast shadows.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Known NPCs

Randal Eaves


☠️ Known Dangers




🔍 Clues or Items Found




🧩 Notes

Location/Blacksmith.title: Blacksmith
Location/Blacksmith.content:
Located near the quarry. Provide tools for mine exchange for iron and copper.
Purpose: purchase or order tools, jewels or custom order.

Location/Grandma-House.title: Grandma House
Location/Grandma-House.content:
Grandma House
Region: Northern edge of town, forested residential outskirts
Access: Unlocked after arrival

📜 Description
An abandoned home at the northern tip of Townia. Though the previous owner passed years ago, the house seems maintained — swept floors, warm air, and the smell of old wood. Charlotte lived here in her childhood. Now it’s a haven — but only for a time. The fog doesn’t quite reach inside… yet.

🧠 Lore / History


Charlotte’s grandmother once lived here and was part of a warding ritual.


Certain rooms seem unaged; a sign that time or memory might be anchored inside.


“This house doesn’t remember me. It remembers _something.”



🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Known NPCs

None (but filled with memories. More than normal)


🔦 Points of Interest


Attic Music Box: Plays a tune from Charlotte’s dreams — not that she remembers.


Photo Wall: One face blurred out in every frame.


Basement Door: Locked tight. Maybe she can find a way somehow.


Garden Patch: Soil smells metallic. Iron rods buried deep.



☠️ Known Dangers


The basement is tight shut. She can’t tell what’s in it


Sleep here too often and dreams begin replacing reality.


A mirror doesn’t reflect fog — but something else.



🔍 Clues or Items Found


Burned Letter: Grandma’s final warning.


Music Box Key: Found beneath floorboard.


Partial Ritual Diagram: Reveals placement of protective glyphs.


Old Sketch of Townia — includes structures that don’t exist anymore.



🧩 Function (Gameplay Purpose)


Player home base / rest area


Unlocks core memories, flashbacks, and ritual history


Only the safe place from the fog — don’t know how long it will last

Location/Lighthouse.title: Lighthouse
Location/Lighthouse.content:
Lighthouse
Type:: Location
Region:: Coastal cliff, the tallest place in the town
Access:: Restricted

📜 Description
Standing tall on the western cliff, the lighthouse is Townia’s highest structure — once a beacon for wayward fishing boats, now a pulsing anomaly. Its light no longer rotates normally; instead, it pulses in deliberate intervals, sometimes flickering to the rhythm of something unseen offshore. The ocean crashes violently below, and no one comes up here unless they must. The path to the lighthouse is steep and exposed, often swallowed by fog. Despite its height, the fog here seems denser than anywhere else in town.

🧠 Lore / History


Randal has not left the tower in over 4 months.


He claims the light “no longer guides — it warns.”


Some nights, the light spins counterclockwise. Some nights… it doesn’t spin at all.


Logs describe phantom ships that follow the beam but vanish before reaching shore.


The structure predates the official founding of Townia. Some suspect it was built atop something else.



🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Known NPCs

Randal Eaves


🔦 Points of Interest


Light Chamber: At the top of the tower; features heavy gears, unstable mechanisms, and glyph carvings beneath rusted panels.


Randal’s Living Quarters: Scattered with torn ship logs, half-functioning radios, and maps covered in red wax markings.


Observation Platform: A narrow balcony with a fogged lens viewer. You may glimpse something crawling along the waves.


Service Hatch: Rusted shut, sealed with a broken keypad. Unlockable later — leads to a maintenance crawlspace or hidden lower floor.



☠️ Known Dangers


Possible dream exposure while sleeping inside.


Reports of time stutter near the observation lens — memories loop or stutter.



🔍 Clues or Items Found


Lighthouse Logbook Pages (collectible; includes Randal’s sightings and timestamps)


Fog Glyph Fragment etched into the lens’ rim


Old Navy Medallion: Bound to Randal’s sanity, used in his side quest or something



🧩 Function (Gameplay Purpose)


Lore and memory unlock zone: visions, audio logs, dream triggers


Used for major story beats (e.g., ship sightings)


The pulse pattern of the light acts as a code or key in several puzzles


Base for Randal, who gives key insights into the fog’s behavior

Location/Logger.title: Logger
Location/Logger.content: Located close by to the farm. A family of 3 lived there, making a living out of wood cutting and carpentry.

Location/Marketplace.title: Marketplace
Location/Marketplace.content:
A gathering place to trade various items. Always busy in the morning. name should change to fish market for unreasonable amount to fish monger.
Purpose: purchase and appraise items

Location/Quarry-Mine.title: Quarry Mine
Location/Quarry-Mine.content:
Region: Western rocky terrain
Access: Open, but deeper sections restricted

📜 Description
The Quarry Mine is still in operation — on the surface. Workers chip away at stone and unearth copper and iron deposits. But deeper within, the tunnels run quiet. The mine’s collapse from months ago is officially labeled a “structural accident,” but many in town suspect otherwise. Old Man Jeofrey, the foreman, keeps work going… and questions to a minimum.

🧠 Lore / History


Ten months ago, a shaft breach revealed something older than stone — a tunnel carved with glyphs.


The collapse was engineered by Jeofrey, who then sealed the breach and resumed normal operations.


Miners report hearing whispers through the rock.


Jeofrey keeps the damaged helmets locked in a shed. One of them is wet on the inside.



🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Known NPCs


Old Man Jeofrey  — Quarry Foreman. Gruff and unshakable. Claims “nothing’s down there.”


Luis (Missing Miner) — Supposedly left town. His locker is still locked. Keys are in Jeofrey’s pocket.



🔦 Points of Interest


Surface Dig Site: Active work zone.


Old Shaft Entrance: Locked and boarded. Marked “UNSTABLE” in red chalk.


Tool Shed: Holds evidence Jeofrey denies exists.


Echo Tunnel: Workers say the rock “calls back in another voice.” Entry is restricted — but not secure.



☠️ Known Dangers


Areas near the sealed shaft distort sound and direction.


Workers have gone home with scratched arms and no memory of how they got hurt.


Reports of breathing rock are dismissed as “airflow pressure.”



🔍 Clues or Items Found


Broken Helmet with interior glyph scratchings


Echo Hammer: When struck, reverberates phrases in Deep Glyph


Jeofrey’s Dossier: Half-burned paper mentioning “replacements in the lower crew”



🧩 Function (Gameplay Purpose)


Lore environment where reality begins to shift


Charlotte may use equipment to record glyph resonance


Optional questline: Confront Jeofrey or protect the town by helping maintain the lie

Location/SeaSight-Tavern.title: SeaSight Tavern
Location/SeaSight-Tavern.content:
Region: Lower town, near coastal path
Access: Always open

📜 Description
A cozy inn nestled near the track to the ocean. Warm lights, old wood, and the ever-present smell of fish stew. The last place that pretends everything is normal. But there are whispers in the kitchen, and the mirror in the dining hall never fogs — no matter how thick the mist outside.

🧠 Lore / History


Built on the foundation of a lifeboat house.


The tavern mirror was salvaged from a wrecked ship. Some believe it sees too much.


The owner’s daughter is the only person still seen cleaning Grandma’s house.



🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Known NPCs

Elias Varn


🔦 Points of Interest


Dining Hall Mirror: Always shows one more person than is present.


Bulletin Board: Gossip and rumors — some shift each day.


Private Room: Rentable room that alters from time to time.


Pantry Door: Locked. Unruly sounds behind it.



☠️ Known Dangers


Replaced NPCs may gather here mid-game.


The mirror sometimes “shows” about the user that they can’t remember.


Eating the wrong dish may trigger hallucinations.



🔍 Clues or Items Found


Cryptic Menu Card: Lists dishes with glyph-based names.


Scratched Wooden Plank: Weirdly attracting



🧩 Function (Gameplay Purpose)


NPC hub, early quest start point


Option to borrow flashlight or gather town rumors

Mechanic/Dying.title: Dying
Mechanic/Dying.content:
For most in Townia, death is a form of escape.
The ultimate freedom.
The release from the fog’s slow suffocation.
Nobody can prevent it.
Everybody will face it.
And, in the end, everyone will give into it.

But Not Charlotte
The moment she stepped into the fog,
It was drawn to her — perhaps because of her dreams, perhaps of simple curiosity, or perhaps for reasons no human could name.
She has dwelled on things she should never have touched.
Followed thoughts she should have left alone.
Looked too long in the fog that were not meant to be understood.
Now she is bound to the fog.
When she dies, it will not free her.
It will pull her deeper.
She is becoming…
a Forgotten.

What Death Means for Charlotte
For her, death is not release.
It is displacement.
She wakes in the wrong day — sometimes in the past, sometimes in the future, sometimes just as usual, sometime in the wrong place.
The town twists around her.
NPCs change. Locations shift. The rules fray.
Every time she returns, the fog holds her a little tighter.
Every time, it is harder to tell what is real.
And every time, the line between Charlotte and the Forgotten grows thinner.

Gameplay
Death is not the end. Never the game over. It is a necessity component. For some outcome, it is a requirement.
When Charlotte die. She wake up, maybe yesterday, maybe today, maybe tomorrow, or maybe sometime. It is always unpredictable. The town is not safe either, something, someone, someplace or some memory may be changed, replaced, distorted, added, or erased.
Dying cause a heavy toll on Charlotte’s mind. It can cause her immense pain and trauma that it would cost her sanity. She may retain the memory, or have blurry visions, even might corrupted by false memories.

Mechanic/Leaving-the-Town.title: Leaving the Town
Mechanic/Leaving-the-Town.content:
Why does Charlotte or other leave the town
At first, there’s no physical barrier.
No wall. No guards. No warning.
The road out is still there.
The bus still runs — at least once in a while.
But no one truly leaves.
They just… stop trying.

The “Leaving Effect”
People who make plans to leave feel fine that day.
They pack, say goodbyes, even head toward the exit.
But by the next morning, they’re still in town.
Their luggage is unpacked.
Their schedule’s forgotten.
They’re convinced they “changed their mind” — but can’t recall why.
"I was going to visit my cousin in the city, but... I guess not. Things to do. You know how it is."

This isn’t mind control.
It’s not force.
It’s resignation.
The fog doesn’t drag people back — it unroots their will.
A person cannot decide to leave. The fog will determine when one need to go.

People Who “Left”
Some townsfolk swear others did leave.

“Old Mira? Took the ferry years ago.”
“Mayor’s brother? Moved inland. I think.”

But no one gets letters.
No one receives calls.
Their names fade from conversation like fog in the wind.
And yet… their houses remain untouched.
Dust-free.
Food still fresh.
As if they might walk back in any second.
Or as if someone is living there.
Some of them do come back. But they feel not the same

What Happens If You Try Anyway?
Some NPCs will try — players may even help.


The next day, they’ll be back.
Tired. Confused. Apologetic.
Their journey will feel like a dream they can’t piece together.
Some may even lose time — waking up a week later with no idea where they were.


Some Forgotten
After they left, no one can remember them. they will straight up deny their existent. It’s like they never exist. Their home, belonging, marking they make and memories, disappear from the town.



Gameplay Hook
Charlotte might be partially resistant.

But every attempt causes a price:
Time shifts.
Sanity spikes.
A day repeats… slightly altered.
She finds herself waking in the same clothes, but her reflection blinks out of sync.
Or waking up with a memory that she can’t remember.

Mechanic/The-Fogbound.title: The Fogbound
Mechanic/The-Fogbound.content:
Origins
The Forgotten were not always monsters.
Once, they were humans — settlers, scholars, and wanderers — who came into contact with the Being.
They never knew its form, never saw its face, never heard its voice as we might understand it.
Instead, it touched their dreams, guiding them with visions of impossible symbols — the Deep Glyphs.
It promised prosperity:

Knowledge beyond human reach.
Power to bend wind and tide.
Protection from the storms that claimed so many lives.

The Being gave them more than survival — it gave them dominion.

The Price
Every gift came with a hidden cost.
The glyphs themselves were a binding — an oath written into the soul.
They became loyal to the Being, not out of devotion, but by the sheer power of the glyphs rewriting the very patterns of their thoughts.
Over time:


Their bodies darkened as if the fog seeped into their blood.


Their forms began to warp — tall and thin like shadows, or heavy and hulking like half-formed nightmares.


They struggled to maintain a human shape, especially in the deep fog.


Their eyes vanished into black pits, their mouths filled with too many teeth — always grinning, always hungry.



Powers
The Forgotten move unnaturally, as though the fog carries them.
They are not bound by normal human limits.


They can vanish into the mist and reappear without sound.


They became one with fog. Their thought are shared by the fog, becoming hive mind like.


They see things no human can — even in the deepest dark.


Their touch carries a mind-haze: those who survive an encounter often forget it happened, or suffer the memory “blinks” common in Townia.

Monster/Coiler.title: Coiler
Monster/Coiler.content:
Type:: Creature / Entity
Classification:: Aquatic Stalker / Ambusher
Threat Level:: High

📜 Description
Being near it feels like drowning on dry land — the air grows thick, wet, and heavy, making every breath a struggle. Moisture beads on your skin, seeping into clothes, clinging until it feels as though the fog itself is trying to pull you under. The scent of brine and decay lingers in its wake.

🧠 Lore / Origin
Once a fisherman of Townia, now an abomination bound to the fog’s will. It is obsessed with catching something — what that “something” is, no one knows. Some say it will leave you alone if it has already claimed its desired prize, though no one who has been caught has returned to confirm this. Old glyphs, carved into stone near the docks, serve as warnings of its presence — crude depictions of tentacles, drowning figures, and the deep.

🧩 Behavior Patterns

Lies motionless in the fog until a target is near, then strikes without warning.
Relocates and “camps” after each successful catch.
The air around it becomes unnaturally damp, leaving behind slick, soggy traces.
Uses tentacles to seize prey, dragging them toward hidden water sources.


🔀 Forms / Stages

Low Fog Density: Difficult to spot, but faint ripples in puddles or water surfaces may give it away.
High Fog Density: Nearly invisible; only a shimmer or distorted air hints at its location.
Sanity Influence: The lower the player’s sanity, the more aggressive it becomes. Severing one of its tentacles causes two to regrow, each faster and stronger.


🗣️ Perception

Player: Can occasionally glimpse its silhouette when it moves in invisibility.
Charlotte: Sees it as a monstrous, amphibious figure with writhing tentacles.
Townsfolk: Attribute disappearances to wild animals or freak accidents at sea.


📍 Known Habitats

Any location with water — wells, beaches, the river, rocky tide pools.
Migratory, following sources of moisture and fog density.


⚠️ Threats / Abilities

Can remain perfectly still in thick fog, becoming effectively invisible.
Produces a sticky, flammable goop that hampers movement.
Can extend tentacles through the fog to snatch prey from a distance.


🛡️ Weaknesses

Fire: The goop coating its body dries quickly when heated and ignites easily.
Environmental Avoidance: Avoiding bodies of water reduces encounter chances.


🎮 Function (Gameplay Purpose)

Acts as an elite predator in the fog, requiring special tactics to counter.
Forces players to manage positioning near water and use environmental hazards.
Ties into environmental clues and glyph warnings for pre-emptive avoidance.


🔍 Clues / Loot

Pools of viscous, unidentifiable slime.
Damaged fishing nets, hooks, and scales not belonging to any known sea creature.


🧩 Notes
Highly territorial, but its “territory” shifts constantly. Survivors speak of hearing water splashing from impossible distances before it strikes.

Concept Art

Monster/Coldman.title: Coldman
Monster/Coldman.content:
Type:: Creature / Entity
Classification:: Fogbound Collector
Threat Level:: low → extreme

📜 Description
A tall, sharply dressed gentleman in a steampunk tailcoat and tophat, walking with a black cane capped in silver. At a glance, he appears human enough — polite posture, fluid movements, even the faint air of nobility. But there’s something wrong: his shadow lags behind, his breath never mists in the cold, and his eyes burn faint red when he glances your way.

🧠 Lore / Origin
No one remembers when Coldman first appeared in Townia — only that he always seems to be where he’s most needed… or least expected. Some whisper he’s a Watcher gone astray, others think he’s the last merchant of the Fogbound, trading not for gold but for something far more personal.
The truth? Coldman is a Collector — a Fogbound entity tasked with gathering memories, knowledge, and fragments of sanity for the Being. His deals feel fair, but each exchange tilts the balance between human and monster… and always in his favor.

🧩 Behavior Patterns

Moves like an ordinary man, always calm and deliberate.
Fights with grace, using melee or ranged attacks based on player position.
The air around him grows unnaturally cold when he’s near.


🔀 Forms / Stages

Merchant Form – Offers goods, quests, or cryptic warnings. Friendly demeanor.
Shifted Form – When Charlotte’s sanity drops or after repeated deals, becomes distant and unnerving. Speech turns sharper.
Final Form – Reveals full Fogbound nature; cane becomes a conduit for freezing fog and shadow-portals.


🗣️ Perception

Player: Feels subtly wrong — shadow out of sync, movement too smooth.
Charlotte: Possibly a Watcher… but his eyes are wrong.
Townsfolk: “Oh, him? Just a traveling gentleman.” “Coldman? Who? Ahh, you mean that gentleman? He didn’t talk much but, he’s a honest trader”


📍 Known Habitats

Wanders Townia after a key event.
Appears in different spots when player is stuck or low on resources.


⚠️ Threats / Abilities

Ice Manipulation – Freezes terrain, slows movement.
Memory Alteration – Erases or distorts small details in the world.
Shadow-Whip Cane – Extends to strike at range, snapping like a serpent.
Portal Hat – Opens small rifts; uses them to attack from unexpected angles or grab the player.
Area Freeze – Slams cane down to instantly frost the ground.


🛡️ Weaknesses


In early game, not aggressive unless provoked.


Vulnerable to heat-based attacks and weapons made out of iron in combat.


Becomes less predictable the more deals the player makes.



🎮 Function (Gameplay Purpose)


Early Game – Friendly NPC, selling supernatural items and providing cryptic hints about anomalies.


Mid Game – Starts testing the player, questioning their motives.


Late Game – Becomes a major boss; difficulty scales with how much you’ve relied on his aid.


The more you die, the more wary and hostile he becomes.



🔍 Clues / Loot


Early: Special consumables, rare lore fragments, quest items.


Boss: Fragment of his cane (weapon upgrade) and a Fog Shard for major story progression.



🧩 Notes


Serves as the player’s most trusted “friend” before becoming one of their most dangerous foes.


Personality is polite and well-spoken, but turns predatory when sanity is low.


A master of calculated patience — lets the player dig their own grave before striking.



Concept Art

Monster/Creeker.title: Creeker
Monster/Creeker.content:
Type:: Creature / Entity
Classification::   Stalker
Threat Level:: Low

📜 Description
Tall, impossibly slender figures with elongated limbs ending in sharp, splinter-like claws. Their movement is accompanied by an unnatural creaking sound — a rhythmic grind like warped wood under strain, produced by grinding their jagged teeth together. They are almost always heard before they are seen, and even then, only at the very edges of perception.

🧠 Lore / Origin
Creekers are remnants of something once human, though their exact origin is unknown. Their forms are unstable, constantly shifting as if reality cannot hold them in place. They cannot be perceived by those fully sane — their presence is a fracture in the mind’s ability to process reality. Only those touched by the fog’s influence, or slipping toward madness, can begin to hear their creaking call.

🧩 Behavior Patterns

Primary Role: Stalker and indirect guide.
Tracks its target from a distance, often without direct confrontation.
Will follow for hours or days before making its move.
Uses sound to mislead or lure prey into certain areas.


🔀 Forms / Stages

Low Sanity: Visible in distorted flashes, moves erratically.
Mid Sanity: Only audible, creaking growing louder the closer it is.
Full Sanity: Completely invisible, sound faint and intermittent — may be mistaken for the environment.


🗣️ Perception

Player: May catch brief visual flickers and directional audio cues.
Charlotte: Hears strange creaking noises but rationalizes them as wind, old wood, or distant construction.
Townsfolk: Rarely notice — if they do, they dismiss it entirely (“old trees shifting in the wind”).


📍 Known Habitats

Prefers wooded areas and places with natural ambient noise to mask its approach.
Migratory, wandering freely around Townia but lingering near glyph sites and deep in forest.


⚠️ Threats / Abilities

Auditory Manipulation: Distorts and misdirects sound to lure prey or cause confusion.
Stalker Persistence: Will trail a target indefinitely until conditions are right to strike.
Psychic Pressure: Prolonged exposure increases paranoia and sanity drain.


🛡️ Weaknesses

Avoidance: If the creaking grows louder, moving in the opposite direction greatly reduces encounter risk.
Glyph wards tuned to sound distortion may repel it temporarily.


🎮 Function (Gameplay Purpose)

At full sanity, acts as a subtle guide, luring the player toward hidden clues or lore objects.
As sanity drops, becomes increasingly hostile, actively hunting and distorting audio cues.
Serves as both a breadcrumb mechanic and an escalating threat — following its sound may lead to rare rewards, but at significant risk.


🔍 Clues / Loot

Deep claw marks carved into tree bark, sometimes forming partial glyphs.
Unnatural creaking sounds that persist even when wind is absent.


🧩 Notes
Its role shifts depending on the player’s mental state — ally, omen, or executioner.

Concept Art

Monster/Crusherjaw.title: Crusherjaw
Monster/Crusherjaw.content:
Type:: Creature / Entity
Classification:: Fogbound Aberration
Threat Level:: Moderate (Boss)

📜 Description
Top-heavy and hulking, Crusherjaw’s silhouette is dominated by a grotesquely oversized right arm, knotted with muscle and thick as a tree trunk. It has no neck; instead, its face is embedded deep in its chest, a gaping mouth lined with jagged, boulder-crushing teeth.
Its left hand is stunted, good only for crude grabs, while a single oversized, unblinking eye bulges from the left side of its head — a rarity among Fogbound. Every step it takes makes the ground quake, scattering dust and loose stone.

🧠 Lore / Origin
Once a miner, desperate to save his trapped child from a quarry collapse. He sought strength where no man should, whispering into the fog for help. The Being answered — and the price was more than he could carry.
Now, Crusherjaw is bound to the quarry, forever “digging” for something only it can see.

🧩 Behavior Patterns

Heavy, thunderous footsteps that shake terrain.
Will not leave its quarry territory, but kills anything that enters it.
Smashes obstacles with overwhelming force, creating new hazards for the player.
Throws debris or chunks of stone when at range.


🔀 Forms / Stages

As it takes damage, fog seeps deeper into its body, swelling its size and amplifying its strength.
Can only be seen if Charlotte’s sanity is below ~20% or if a special artifact/glyph is active.


🗣️ Perception

Player: A living wall of muscle and stone, its movements shaking the screen.
Charlotte: A nightmare given form, a monster she must defeat to press onward.
Townsfolk: Claim “there’s nothing down in the quarry” — they’ve never seen it.


📍 Known Habitats

Deep within the rocky quarry mine.
Highly territorial — will never leave its home.


⚠️ Threats / Abilities

Sheer Strength — crushes rock, wood, or metal alike.
Terrain Destruction — alters the battlefield mid-fight, creating hazards and bottlenecks.
Pursuit — slow but relentless; once it gives chase, it won’t stop until you leave its range or kill it.


🛡️ Weaknesses

Repelled by wards and safe zones.
Vulnerable to iron tools — steel slides harmlessly from its hide.
Best counter: stay out of range; run, don’t hide.


🎮 Function (Gameplay Purpose)

Serves as a major boss and a hard roadblock.
Forces the player to learn about Enchantment Glyphs to progress.
Breaks walls and environmental barriers to corner the player.
Optional clue: understanding the glyph will help to counter it.


🔍 Clues / Loot

Body is tattooed with ancient glyphs granting strength enhancement.
Dropped loot: a fragment of its glyph-skin, usable to unlock a glyph deciphering.


🧩 Notes

Only boss-level Fogbound have visible eyes — a sign they still “see” their prey directly.
Encounters should feel like being trapped in a collapsing quarry.

Town.title: Town
Town.content:
Townia, a port town built at the coastal valley. Sink toward to deep shoreline with an ocean filled with coastal and giant rock. Small boat won’t never have a chance to break through the wave, and the large one, halted by reef. The shore is covered by large mountain range from both east and west. Caves and caverns are form which too dangerous to explore.
Townia located at primary east side of the shore, with a beaming lighthouse on a cliff at west. A river ran across the town to the sea flowing from the mountains. A rocky terrain is present at the west of the town, supplying with quarry for building materials.
Townia has small population of about 300, with not much tourist footprint. people make a living out of shellfish from sea and fishing in river. It’s usually sunny and windy ith frequent rainstorm. there’re windmill at the outskirt of the town, provide enough electricity for the whole town. There’s a farm to the east of the town, providing with wheat and vegetation with their own watermill..
